sentence: 姐姐教我系鞋带，我练了几次终于学会了，现在能自己系了。
grammar: 会 follows 学 to mark successful acquisition of a skill. It differs from preverbal 会 expressing an existing ability.
note: 系鞋带 jì xiédài means tie shoelaces; 系 is read jì here.

sentence: 这两份工作，一份工资高但离家远，一份工资低但离家近；我想透了，决定选近的，多留点时间陪家人。
grammar: 透 after 想 expresses reaching a thorough understanding of the considerations involved, beyond merely thinking about them.
note: 工资 gōngzī means salary; 留 liú here means keep or leave available.

sentence: 我收拾桌子时弄丢了钥匙，桌面和抽屉都找过了，还是没找到。
grammar: 丢 follows the general handling verb 弄 and states the unintended loss resulting from that handling.
note: 弄 nòng means do or handle something; 桌面 zhuōmiàn means tabletop; 抽屉 chōuti means drawer. 还是 háishi here means still, despite the unsuccessful search.

sentence: 电话里，姐姐说了见面的时间和地点，我听漏了地点，只记住了下午三点。
grammar: 漏 after 听 identifies information missed during listening. The time was retained, but the location was missed.
note: 地点 dìdiǎn means location or meeting place.

sentence: 弟弟推倒了椅子，椅子横在地上；我扶起来，重新放好。
grammar: 倒 after 推 marks the chair falling over because of the push. This is dǎo, distinct from pouring dào.
note: 横 héng here describes lying across a surface; 扶起来 fú qǐlai means help or steady something back upright.

sentence: 那几天夜里很冷，我没把阳台上的花搬进屋，结果花冻死了，后来只好扔掉。
grammar: 死 follows 冻 and states death resulting from exposure to severe cold.
note: 冻 dòng means freeze or be affected by severe cold; 屋 wū means a room or house.

sentence: 这盆花原来快死了，妈妈没放弃，终于救活了它，现在又长出了新叶子。
grammar: 活 after 救 marks successful rescue from impending death. It does not require the plant to have already died.
note: 救 jiù means rescue or save; 新叶子 xīn yèzi means new leaves.

sentence: 弟弟往盆里倒水，水把排成一行的小纸船冲散了，几只漂到了左边，几只漂到了右边。
grammar: 散 after 冲 marks the arranged boats becoming separated through the movement of water.
note: 冲 chōng here means sweep along with flowing water; 纸船 zhǐchuán means paper boat; 漂 piāo means float. 排成一行 páichéng yī háng means arrange in a row.

sentence: 我修椅子时用尽了最后一瓶胶水，瓶里一点也没有了。
grammar: 尽 after 用 marks exhaustion of the available supply. It provides another lexical way to express complete consumption.
note: 用 yòng here means use; 胶水 jiāoshuǐ means glue.

sentence: 我翻遍了家里所有的抽屉，连最小的那个也找过了，还是没找到钥匙。
grammar: 遍 follows 翻 and expresses searching throughout every drawer. Unlike 一遍, it does not count one complete repetition.
note: 翻 fān here means rummage through; 所有 suǒyǒu means all. 连……也…… lián…yě… means even, highlighting an unexpected or extreme member of a set.

sentence: 我拿盐时打翻了汤碗，汤全洒在桌子上了，碗没有破。
grammar: 翻 after 打 marks overturning caused by a knock. The spilled soup and intact bowl distinguish overturning from breakage.
note: 打 dǎ here means knock; 汤碗 tāngwǎn means soup bowl; 洒 sǎ means spill or scatter.

sentence: 公交车还停着，爷爷扶着座位坐稳了，不再摇晃，司机这才开车。
grammar: 稳 after 坐 marks attaining a secure seated position, rather than simply being seated.
note: 座位 zuòwèi means seat; 司机 sījī means driver. 开 kāi means drive in 开车.

sentence: 我用绳子把箱子绑牢了，又用力拉了几下，绳结还是紧的。
grammar: 牢 after 绑 emphasizes fastening that stays secure. The knot remains fast despite the subsequent pulls.
note: 绑 bǎng means tie or bind; 绳结 shéngjié means knot in a cord.

sentence: 我在桌子下面找鞋，站起来时撞疼了额头，就用手揉了揉。
grammar: 疼 follows 撞 and states the painful condition caused in the affected body part, 额头.
note: 撞 zhuàng means bump into; 额头 étóu means forehead; 揉 róu here means rub gently.

sentence: 我在公园跑了半个小时，跑累了，就坐在门口休息。
grammar: 累 follows 跑 and describes fatigue resulting from running. The resulting state belongs to the runner.

sentence: 土豆原来很硬，妈妈煮软以后，我用勺子一按就分开了。
grammar: 软 after 煮 specifies softening achieved through cooking in liquid, rather than merely stating that the food is cooked.
note: 煮 zhǔ means boil or cook in liquid.

sentence: 这块面包在冰箱的冷冻室里放了一夜，冻硬了，用手按也不变形。
grammar: 硬 after 冻 marks hardening caused by freezing. The bread's resistance to pressure describes its resulting condition.
note: 冰箱 bīngxiāng means refrigerator; 冷冻室 lěngdòngshì means freezer compartment; 变形 biànxíng means change shape.

sentence: 我吃饱了，碗里还剩两个饺子，留着晚上再吃吧。
grammar: 饱 after 吃 marks attaining satiety through eating. Food can remain even though the eater has had enough.
note: 剩 shèng means remain; 留着 liúzhe here means keep for later.

sentence: 这周午饭天天吃面，我吃腻了；我还饿，但今天想吃米饭。
meaning: tired of eating the same food
grammar: 腻 after 吃 expresses losing interest in a food through repeated consumption. Remaining hunger distinguishes this from satiety.
note: 天天 tiāntiān means every day.

sentence: 杯子从桌上掉了下来，摔碎了，地上有好几块玻璃。
grammar: 碎 after 摔 specifies fragmentation resulting from a fall or impact.
note: 摔 shuāi means fall heavily; 玻璃 bōli means glass.

sentence: 我烤面包时忘了看时间，面包烤焦了，表面黑了一大片。
grammar: 焦 after 烤 marks charring from excessive heating, rather than successful cooking or readiness.
note: 烤 kǎo means bake or roast; 表面 biǎomiàn means surface.

sentence: 锅里的土豆煮得太久，煮烂了，我一搅就全散了，原来的块已经没有了。
meaning: cooked until soft and falling apart
grammar: 烂 after 煮 describes food becoming so soft that its pieces break down. Here it does not mean rotten.

sentence: 这根绳子原来弯着，我用两只手拉直了，才量它有多长。
grammar: 直 after 拉 marks straightening caused by pulling. The cord's earlier bent shape supplies the contrast.
note: 弯 wān means bent or curved.

sentence: 我用手铺平了床单，上面一个褶子也没有了。
grammar: 平 after 铺 specifies the flat, smooth condition achieved by spreading the sheet.
note: 铺 pū means spread or lay out; 床单 chuángdān means bedsheet; 褶子 zhězi means fold or crease.

sentence: 刚才我们还大声说话；孩子睡着以后，我们压低了声音，只让旁边的人听见。
grammar: 低 after 压 marks a reduction in level. In 压低声音, the level is voice volume rather than physical height.
note: 压 yā means press down; 压低声音 yādī shēngyīn means lower one's voice.

sentence: 我们在桌腿下面加了木块，抬高了桌面；桌面原来离地七十厘米，现在是七十五厘米。
grammar: 高 after 抬 marks an increase in physical height. The before-and-after measurements establish the change.
note: 抬 tái means lift or raise; 木块 mùkuài means wooden block; 桌腿 zhuōtuǐ means table leg.

sentence: 种树的坑太浅，我又挖深了十厘米，树根现在全在土里了。
grammar: 深 after 挖 marks increasing the pit's depth. 十厘米 gives the additional depth, not the final total.
note: 种树 zhòng shù means plant a tree; 树根 shùgēn means tree roots.

sentence: 椅子离桌子太远，我拉近了椅子，现在坐着就能拿到桌上的书。
grammar: 近 after 拉 marks reducing the distance by pulling. The table remains the reference point.

sentence: 我想把球扔给两米外的弟弟，结果扔远了，球落在十米外的草地上。
grammar: 远 after 扔 marks the achieved distance of the throw. Here the actual endpoint exceeds the intended recipient's distance.
note: 落 luò here means land; 草地 cǎodì means grass-covered ground or lawn.

sentence: 这段录音说得太慢，我调快了播放速度，原来十分钟的内容现在八分钟就放完了。
grammar: 快 after 调 marks an increased speed resulting from an adjustment.
note: 调 tiáo means adjust; 录音 lùyīn means recording; 播放 bōfàng means play recorded material.

sentence: 爷爷走得有点吃力，我放慢了脚步，陪着他一起往前走。
grammar: 慢 after 放 marks a reduction in pace. 放慢脚步 describes slowing one's steps while continuing to walk.
note: 吃力 chīlì means requiring effort; 脚步 jiǎobù means steps or walking pace.

sentence: 门关着，我敲响了门边的小铃，妈妈听见铃声就来开门了。
grammar: 响 after 敲 marks sound successfully produced by striking. The mother's response confirms that the bell was heard.
note: 铃 líng means bell; 铃声 língshēng means the sound of a bell.

sentence: 那把旧勺子原来暗暗的，我用布擦亮了，现在能在上面看见自己的脸。
grammar: 亮 after 擦 marks a shining surface produced by polishing, rather than the brightness of a light source.
note: 布 bù means cloth.

sentence: 手很冷，我把双手放在衣服里捂热了，才拿出来写字。
grammar: 热 after 捂 marks warming achieved by keeping something covered.
note: 捂 wǔ means cover or keep enclosed; 双手 shuāngshǒu means both hands.

sentence: 粥刚煮好时烫嘴，我放在桌上晾凉了才喝。
grammar: 凉 after 晾 marks cooling achieved by leaving something exposed to the air. Here 晾 concerns cooling, not drying clothes.
note: 粥 zhōu means porridge; 烫嘴 tàngzuǐ means uncomfortably hot to the mouth. 晾 is read liàng, while result 凉 is liáng.

sentence: 我在原地转了十几圈，转晕了，停下以后还觉得屋子在转，只好扶着椅子。
grammar: 晕 after 转 marks dizziness caused by spinning. The affected person is the subject.
note: 原地 yuándì means in the same spot; 转 zhuàn means spin; 圈 quān counts turns. 晕 is yūn for feeling dizzy here, distinct from yùn in motion-sickness words.

sentence: 放学后，孩子等妈妈来接，等了一个小时还没见到她，急哭了，脸上都是眼泪。
grammar: 哭 follows the anxious state 急 and expresses crying brought on by that distress.
note: 急 jí here means anxious or distressed; 放学 fàngxué means finish school for the day.

sentence: 爸爸拿勺子当话筒唱歌，逗笑了孩子；孩子拍着手说：“再唱一次！”
grammar: 笑 after 逗 marks laughter actually elicited from the person being entertained.
note: 当 dàng here means use as; 话筒 huàtǒng means microphone; 拍手 pāishǒu means clap one's hands.

sentence: 我昨天离开时，房间里还是空的；今天回来，看见满屋的花，看愣了，站在门口半天没说话。
grammar: 愣 after 看 expresses becoming stunned by what one sees, with a halt in one's response.
note: 满屋 mǎn wū means throughout the room or filling the room. 半天 bàntiān here means quite a while, not a measured half-day.

sentence: 我以为三点出发，姐姐却说三点见面；问过她以后，终于弄明白了：三点在车站见，三点半才上车。
grammar: 明白 follows 弄 and marks resolving confusion through inquiry. The second syllable bai is neutral-tone.
note: 出发 chūfā means set off; 却 què marks a contrast with the preceding expectation. 弄 nòng is a general action verb in 弄明白, figure out.

sentence: 弟弟戴着两顶帽子走进教室，大家一看就笑起来了，连老师也笑了。
grammar: 起来 after 笑 marks the onset of laughter, without upward movement.
note: 连……也…… lián…yě… means even, highlighting the teacher's participation.

sentence: 早上出门还很冷，到了中午，天气暖和起来了，我脱了外套。
grammar: 起来 after 暖和 presents the emergence of a warmer state, rather than the onset of an action.
note: 暖和 nuǎnhuo means comfortably warm; 脱 tuō means take off clothing.

sentence: 我刚才不记得那家店的名字，看到旧收据才想起来：叫“绿叶”。
grammar: 起来 after 想 marks retrieving something previously known.
note: 旧收据 jiù shōujù means an old receipt; 绿叶 Lǜyè is the fictional shop name.

sentence: 我给妹妹买了生日礼物，已经藏起来了，就放在床下的箱子里，她还没发现。
grammar: 起来 after 藏 presents putting something away where it remains concealed. It does not specify upward movement.
note: 藏 cáng means hide; 生日礼物 shēngrì lǐwù means birthday present.

sentence: 这两袋苹果，一袋三斤，一袋两斤，加起来一共五斤。
grammar: 起来 after 加 brings the separately stated amounts together into one total.
note: 加 jiā means add; 加起来 jiā qǐlai means add together.

sentence: 这把椅子腿很细，看起来不太结实，不过我坐了几次，都很稳。
grammar: 看起来 introduces an impression based on appearance. The later sitting experience qualifies that initial impression.
note: 结实 jiēshi means sturdy; 稳 wěn means stable or securely balanced.

sentence: “桌子往左挪半米，这里就能多放两把椅子。”“听起来不错，我们试试。”
grammar: 听起来 introduces an assessment of what has been said. Here it evaluates the explicit proposal, rather than a voice or accent.
note: 挪 nuó means shift something a short distance.

sentence: 这把剪刀我刚试过，用起来很省力，厚纸也很容易剪。
grammar: 用起来 evaluates the experience of using an item. 用 is the action verb use here, rather than an instrumental preposition.
note: 省力 shěnglì means require little physical effort; 剪 jiǎn means cut with scissors.

sentence: 老师停止播放录音，大家也不再说话，教室终于安静下来了。
grammar: 下来 after 安静 presents the transition into a settled quiet state, without literal descent.
note: 停止 tíngzhǐ means stop; 播放 bōfàng means play recorded material.

sentence: 姐姐说：“明天三点在图书馆门口见。”我怕忘记，就在本子上记下来了。
grammar: 记下来 means make an external record for later reference. The notebook distinguishes this from retaining information mentally with 记住.
note: 本子 běnzi means notebook; 记 jì here means record in writing.

sentence: 那门课每天都要练一个小时，虽然很累，我还是坚持下来了，昨天上完了最后一节课。
grammar: 坚持下来 presents perseverance through a difficult period up to an endpoint already reached. The final class has been completed.
note: 坚持 jiānchí means persevere; 门 mén counts courses, and 节 jié counts class sessions.

sentence: 我写的故事里，那本食谱是外婆传下来的：外婆交给妈妈，妈妈后来又交给女儿。
grammar: 传下来 describes transmission from an older generation to younger generations. The family sequence supplies the direction of transmission.
note: 传 chuán means pass on; 食谱 shípǔ means recipe book or collection of recipes.

sentence: “你刚说到在车站发现手机不见了，后来呢？”“我说下去吧：后来我借了别人的电话，给家里打了电话。”
grammar: 下去 after 说 presents continuation beyond the current point in an account, rather than downward movement.
note: 不见了 bù jiàn le here means has gone missing.

sentence: 书我才读了一半，还有三天就要还了；虽然每天很忙，我也要坚持下去，每晚读二十页。
grammar: 坚持下去 commits to continuing effort beyond now. Unlike 坚持下来, it does not present the task's endpoint as already reached.
note: 页 yè means page; 还 huán here means return a borrowed item.

sentence: 照片里那个人的脸不太清楚，但她戴着姐姐每天用的那副红眼镜，我还是认出来了，是姐姐。
grammar: 出来 after 认 marks successful identification from a distinguishing clue. It does not describe physical emergence.
note: 认 rèn means recognize or identify; 副 fù counts a complete set of glasses.

sentence: 约好的是星期一，他刚才却说“星期天见”；我一听就听出来了，日期说错了。
grammar: 听出来 marks detecting something through hearing. Here the listener detects a date mismatch, beyond merely hearing the words clearly.
note: 约好 yuēhǎo means reach an arrangement; 却 què marks contrast.

sentence: 客人要来，家里只有两把椅子；我终于想出来一个办法：去邻居家借两把。
grammar: 想出来 expresses producing an idea through thought. 想起来 instead retrieves something previously known.
note: 办法 bànfǎ means a way to solve a problem; 邻居 línjū means neighbour.

sentence: 大家都想坐公交车，我一直没说自己的意见，后来终于说出来了：“我觉得地铁更快，还是坐地铁吧。”
grammar: 说出来 presents a previously unexpressed thought becoming articulated speech. The quotation gives the opinion actually expressed.
note: 还是 háishi before the proposed choice here means on balance or better.

sentence: 我试了红、黄、蓝三件外套，只有蓝色那件合身，就挑出来放在一边，准备买它。
meaning: out from a set by selection
grammar: 出来 after 挑 marks selecting a member from a set. The fit criterion and selected blue coat are explicit.
note: 挑 tiāo means select; 合身 héshēn means fit the body well.

sentence: 原来只有我、妈妈和弟弟知道要搬家的事，弟弟传出去了，现在亲戚们也都知道了。
grammar: 传出去 describes information spreading beyond its original audience. The relatives form the newly informed group.
note: 亲戚 qīnqi means relatives.

sentence: 弟弟趴在桌上睡着了，我叫了他几声，他才醒过来，抬头问：“几点了？”
grammar: 过来 after 醒 marks a return to awareness. It does not describe crossing toward the speaker.
note: 醒 xǐng means wake or regain awareness; 声 shēng counts calls or other individual sounds.

sentence: 朋友说这次参观免费，我以为午饭也不用付钱，听他解释完才明白过来：只是门票不收钱，午饭要自己买。
grammar: 明白过来 presents a shift from a mistaken assumption to understanding. This is a cognitive extension of 过来.
note: 免费 miǎnfèi means free of charge.

sentence: 他站着跟我说话，忽然晕过去了，倒在地上；我叫他的名字，他没有反应，过了一会儿才睁开眼。
grammar: 晕过去 expresses losing consciousness, rather than merely feeling dizzy. 过去 here is an extended complement, not a time noun.
note: 晕 is yūn here; 倒 dǎo means fall over; 反应 fǎnyìng means response; 睁开眼 zhēngkāi yǎn means open one's eyes.

sentence: 搬家前那几天，白天上班，晚上还要收拾到很晚；终于熬过去了，现在新家都整理好了，可以好好休息。
grammar: 熬过去 presents enduring a difficult period until it has passed. The completed move and present rest establish the endpoint.
note: 熬 áo here means endure a difficult time.

sentence: 以前我不喜欢做饭，跟妈妈学了几次以后，慢慢爱上了做饭，现在周末总想试一道新菜。
grammar: 上 after 爱 marks developing a lasting liking for something. The object can be an activity, not only a person.
note: 爱 ài here means love or be very fond of; 道 dào counts prepared dishes.

sentence: 我给姐姐打了三次电话都没人接，刚才终于联系上了，她在电话里告诉我明天回来。
grammar: 上 after 联系 marks successfully establishing contact. The sister's spoken reply confirms two-way communication without implying agreement to a proposal.
note: 没人接 méi rén jiē means nobody answered the phone.

sentence: 火车八点出发，我七点五十八分赶上了这班车，现在已经坐在车厢里，车还没开。
grammar: 上 after 赶 marks successfully catching the scheduled service. The departure time and achieved seat establish success.
note: 赶 gǎn here means hurry to catch; 车厢 chēxiāng means train carriage; 班 bān counts scheduled services.

sentence: 我们刚才还在商量哪天去，后来都同意星期六，日期就定下来了；大家已经买好了那天的车票。
grammar: 定下来 presents an unresolved arrangement becoming settled. Shared agreement and subsequent ticket purchases establish commitment.
note: 定 dìng here means fix or settle an arrangement; 商量 shāngliang means discuss an arrangement.

sentence: 没买到那场演出的票，我昨天很失望，今天想开了：这次没票，就等下次再看吧。
grammar: 开 in 想开 expresses ceasing to dwell on something disappointing or unchangeable. It does not describe physically opening or separating something.
note: 演出 yǎnchū means performance; 失望 shīwàng means disappointed.

sentence: 这个号码我以前记得很清楚，几年没用，已经忘掉了，现在只好去问姐姐。
grammar: 掉 after 忘 presents loss from memory. 忘掉 is another lexical expression for forgetting, alongside 忘记.
note: 忘 wàng means forget.

sentence: 我在车库里面等，爸爸把车开进来了，现在车就停在我旁边。
grammar: 开 names driving the vehicle. 进来 supplies the inward path toward the speaker waiting inside.
note: 车库 chēkù means garage.

sentence: 前面的路有个大水坑，妈妈绕过去了，从水坑右边走到另一头，鞋一点也没湿。
grammar: 绕 names a route around an obstruction. The path along the puddle's right side distinguishes it from movement through the puddle.
note: 水坑 shuǐkēng means puddle or water-filled hollow.

sentence: 我留在门口，爸爸从我身边进了屋，仍然面朝屋里；里面太挤，他没转身，就退回来了，又站到我旁边。
grammar: 退 specifies backward movement. 回来 supplies return toward the speaker; keeping the same facing direction makes the backward path explicit.
note: 面朝 miàn cháo means face toward; 挤 jǐ here means crowded.

sentence: 照片的背面朝着我，我想看正面，姐姐就把它翻过来了，现在我看见了照片上的人。
grammar: 过来 after 翻 marks turning the object so its other face is presented toward the observer, without carrying it across a space.
note: 背面 bèimiàn means reverse side; 正面 zhèngmiàn means front side; 翻 fān here means turn over.

sentence: 爸爸原来面朝我，听到身后的敲门声，就转过去了，背对着我，朝门口走。
grammar: 过去 after 转 marks reorientation away from the observer. The father's front initially faces the speaker, and his back faces the speaker afterward.
note: 转 is zhuǎn for changing orientation here, contrasting with spinning zhuàn; 背对 bèi duì means have one's back toward.

sentence: 院门关着，小猫从院外翻过矮墙进来了，落在院里的草地上；我就站在墙边看着。
grammar: 翻 names climbing over a barrier, and 过 marks the path across its top to the other side. This differs from resultative 翻 meaning overturned.
note: 院 yuàn means courtyard; 矮墙 ǎi qiáng means low wall. 进来 points toward the speaker inside the courtyard.

sentence: 我站在斜板顶端，松开手，小木块就滑下了斜板，最后停在地上的毛巾上。
grammar: 滑 names sliding motion, and 下 marks the downward path off the inclined board.
note: 斜板 xiébǎn means inclined board; 顶端 dǐngduān means upper end; 毛巾 máojīn means towel. 松开手 sōngkāi shǒu means release one's grip.

sentence: 姐姐要开门，钥匙却在我包里；我取出钥匙递给她，她接过以后就去开门了。
grammar: 取出 combines taking an item with an outward path from its container. The bag is the source, and the keys are the extracted object.
note: 接过 jiēguò here means take an item handed over by someone.

sentence: 姐姐从北京寄来她的字典借我用，我昨天用完就寄回北京了，收件人还是姐姐。
grammar: 寄回 combines mailing with return to an established origin. The sister is both the original sender and the return recipient in Beijing.
note: 收件人 shōujiànrén means recipient of a mailed item.

sentence: 我站在屋里，从开着的窗户探出头，看楼下的孩子踢球，身子还留在屋里。
grammar: 探出 describes extending a body part outward. The head crosses the window opening while the person's body remains inside.
note: 探 tàn here means extend forward or outward; 身子 shēnzi means body.

sentence: 这台电脑昨天坏了，爸爸今天修好了，我刚用它写完作业。
grammar: 好 after 修 specifies a successful repair that restores the device to working condition.
note: 修 xiū means repair.

sentence: 我去超市买牛奶，没约任何人，却在门口碰到老同学，就跟他聊了几句。
grammar: 碰到 here describes an unexpected encounter with a person, rather than physical collision.
note: 老同学 lǎo tóngxué means a former classmate; 聊 liáo means chat.

sentence: 门外突然有人说话，我听见了声音，但隔着门没听懂他说什么。
grammar: 听见 expresses successful auditory perception. Hearing a voice does not necessarily entail understanding its words.
note: 隔 gé here means be separated by; 隔着门 means with the door between the listener and speaker.

sentence: 姐姐准备了一年，今年终于考上了自己想去的大学，已经收到了录取通知。
grammar: 上 after 考 marks attaining admission through examination, rather than physical ascent.
note: 考 kǎo means take an examination; 大学 dàxué means university; 录取通知 lùqǔ tōngzhī means admission notice.

sentence: 这个箱子看着小，却装下了六件厚外套，盖子也合上了。
grammar: 下 after 装 marks successfully fitting the stated contents inside. It does not require filling the container to its rim.
note: 盖子 gàizi means lid; 合 hé means close or bring together.

sentence: 爸爸开车带我进院子时，一个球从旁边滚来；他刹住了车，车停在球前。
grammar: 住 after 刹 marks bringing the moving vehicle to a stop, rather than grasping an object or retaining information.
note: 刹 is shā for braking here.

sentence: 妹妹问我：“我们第一次来这家店是哪一天？”这个问题问住了我，我想了很久，也没想起来。
grammar: 住 after 问 expresses leaving someone stumped by a question. The person questioned is the affected object.

sentence: 桌上只剩一块面包，我用两只手掰开了，和弟弟一人一半。
grammar: 掰开 combines hand-driven breaking with achieved separation into parts.
note: 掰 bāi means break apart with the hands.

sentence: 电脑里的名单上，姐姐的名字写了两次；我删掉了第二个，现在她的名字只出现一次。
meaning: delete; remove from a text or list
grammar: 删掉 expresses actual removal of written or digital content. Here the duplicate entry is removed.
note: 名单 míngdān means list of names; 出现 chūxiàn means appear.

sentence: 我想买三本书，每本二十元，算出一共要付六十元，就带了六十元去书店。
grammar: 出 after 算 marks obtaining a numerical answer through calculation, rather than checking whether an answer is correct.
note: 书店 shūdiàn means bookshop.

sentence: 这两碗汤颜色一样，我各尝了一口，尝出只有右边那碗放了姜。
grammar: 出 after 尝 marks identifying something from its taste. Tasting alone does not necessarily yield that identification.
note: 各 gè means each here.

sentence: 我把几块冰放在盘子里，过了一会儿，冰都变成了水。
meaning: into a resulting material or state
grammar: 成 after 变 introduces the material or state resulting from a change. The ice becomes water.
note: 冰 bīng means ice; 变 biàn means change.

sentence: 通知上写的是“六点”，我看成了“九点”；姐姐提醒后，我改了手机里的时间。
grammar: 成 after 看 introduces the identity assigned to what is seen. Here six is misread as nine; the writing itself does not change.
note: 通知 tōngzhī here means a written notice.

sentence: 这只是一次练习，不算考试；我把它当成发现问题的机会，做错了就问老师。
grammar: 把 A 当成 B presents A as being treated or regarded as B, without requiring a physical transformation or mistaken identity.
note: 机会 jīhuì means opportunity; 不算 bù suàn here means does not count as.

sentence: 这间房就在大路边，刚搬来时我总觉得太吵；住了半年，已经住惯了，晚上也能睡得很好。
grammar: 惯 after 住 marks becoming accustomed to the living conditions through experience, beyond merely residing there.
note: 大路 dàlù means main road.

sentence: 弟弟在沙发上睡觉，楼下突然响了一声车喇叭，把他吓醒了；他坐起来问：“什么声音？”
grammar: 吓 supplies the startling cause in 吓醒. 醒 specifies the awakening that actually results.
note: 沙发 shāfā means sofa; 喇叭 lǎba here means vehicle horn.

sentence: 这两把钥匙我以前总弄混；现在分清了：圆头的开家门，方头的开办公室门。
grammar: 清 after 分 marks successfully distinguishing confusable items. The different head shapes identify the two keys.
note: 弄混 nònghùn means mix up; 圆 yuán means round; 方 fāng here means square.

sentence: 桌上的相框原来向左歪着，我把它摆正了，现在上面的两个角一样高。
grammar: 正 after 摆 specifies corrected physical alignment. It concerns the frame's orientation rather than numerical correctness.
note: 相框 xiàngkuàng means picture frame; 歪 wāi means crooked; 摆 bǎi means place or position; 角 jiǎo means corner here.

sentence: 妹妹的头发原来打着结，妈妈用梳子梳顺了，现在从上往下梳都很轻松。
grammar: 顺 after 梳 describes hair becoming smooth and untangled through combing.
note: 头发 tóufa means hair; 梳 shū means comb; 梳子 shūzi is a comb; 打结 dǎ jié means become knotted or tangled.

sentence: 这几张纸的底边不在一条线上，我用剪刀剪齐了，现在叠在一起，底边正好对上。
grammar: 齐 after 剪 marks trimming edges into alignment, rather than flattening a surface.
note: 底边 dǐbiān means bottom edge; 叠 dié means stack or place in layers.

sentence: 碗里的盐都在一边，我用筷子把盐和蔬菜拌匀了，每一口的咸味都差不多。
grammar: 匀 after 拌 specifies even distribution achieved through mixing, beyond performing the mixing action.
note: 咸味 xiánwèi means salty taste; 差不多 chàbuduō means about the same.

sentence: 毛巾刚洗过，还滴着水；在太阳底下晒了一下午，已经晒干了，摸着一点儿也不湿。
grammar: 干 after 晒 marks dryness achieved through sun exposure. This is gān, distinct from gàn meaning do or work.
note: 太阳 tàiyáng means sun; 滴 dī means drip.

sentence: 雨很大，我从车站走回家时衣服湿透了，外套和里面的衬衫全是水。
grammar: 透 after 湿 expresses thorough saturation. Both the outer coat and the shirt underneath are wet.
note: 衬衫 chènshān means shirt.

sentence: 弟弟踩在空纸盒上，把它压扁了，盒子的上下两面贴在了一起。
grammar: 扁 after 压 marks loss of depth through pressure, rather than smoothing an already broad surface.
note: 踩 cǎi means step on; 纸盒 zhǐhé means cardboard box; 压 yā means press.

sentence: 这根细铁丝原来是直的，我用手折弯了，做成一个小钩子，没有折断。
grammar: 弯 after 折 specifies bending a formerly straight object. The wire remains in one piece.
note: 铁丝 tiěsī means iron wire; 折 zhé here means bend; 钩子 gōuzi means hook.

sentence: 瓶盖太紧，我反着转了两圈，终于拧松了，现在轻轻一转就能打开。
grammar: 松 after 拧 marks loosening achieved by twisting, contrasting with tightening in 拧紧.
note: 拧 is nǐng for turning a cap; 转 is zhuàn for rotation here; 反 fǎn indicates the reverse direction.

sentence: 这杯果汁太甜，我加了半杯水，冲淡以后喝着没那么甜了。
grammar: 淡 after 冲 marks dilution achieved by adding water. Here the reduced concentration also reduces perceived sweetness.
note: 冲 chōng here means dilute by adding water.

sentence: 锅里的汤原来有四碗，妈妈用小火慢慢熬，只剩两碗时已经熬浓了，味道比刚才重。
grammar: 浓 after 熬 marks increased concentration as liquid is reduced. 熬 describes slow cooking here.
note: 熬 áo here means simmer slowly; 小火 xiǎohuǒ means low heat; 味道重 wèidao zhòng means strong in flavor.

sentence: 手机上的合照太小，我把照片放大了，现在每个人的脸都很清楚。
grammar: 大 after 放 marks magnification of the displayed image, rather than independently describing its size.
note: 合照 hézhào means group photograph.

sentence: 文档里的照片原来占了整页，我把它缩小了，现在只占上半页，下面留着写说明。
grammar: 小 after 缩 marks reducing the image's displayed size. The change leaves part of the page available for text.
note: 文档 wéndàng means document; 缩 suō means reduce in size; 占 zhàn means occupy.

sentence: 这家店今天只做了五十个包子，中午就卖完了；我下午去买，老板说一个也没有了。
meaning: sell the entire stock; sell out
grammar: 卖完 expresses completion of selling a bounded stock. Here all fifty buns have been sold.

sentence: 我带了一百元去买书，两本书各五十元，正好花光了，回家时一分钱也没剩。
meaning: spend all of an available sum
grammar: 花光 combines spending with exhaustion of the available money. The two purchases use the entire hundred yuan.

sentence: 我刚才把顺序说反了；理顺以后，我重新讲：先在车站发现没带票，再回家取票，最后上车。
grammar: 理顺 describes organizing relations or a sequence so they become coherent. Here it restores the events' chronological order.
note: 理 lǐ means organize here; 说反 shuōfǎn means state in the reverse order.

sentence: 我昨天丢了钥匙，今天终于找回了：同事在办公室捡到后交给我，现在就在我手里。
meaning: back into the former possessor's hands
grammar: 回 after 找 marks recovery of something lost. The keys are restored to their former possessor, beyond merely locating them.

sentence: 我以前上课总忘带作业；现在写完就放进书包，改掉了这个习惯，最近一个月一次也没忘。
grammar: 改掉 expresses successfully discontinuing an unwanted established practice. The month without another omission establishes the change.
note: 习惯 xíguàn means habit; 最近 zuìjìn means recently.

sentence: 我和朋友吵了一架，他说：“以后别联系我了。”后来就切断了联系，不接我的电话，也不回消息。
grammar: 断 after 切 marks severance of an interpersonal connection. The friend explicitly ends contact and then stops responding.
note: 切 qiē here means cut off; 回消息 huí xiāoxi means reply to a message.

sentence: 门已经关好，但还没锁；我用钥匙锁上了门，才离开办公室。
grammar: 锁上 presents locking as an achieved result. A door can already be closed while its lock remains unsecured.
note: 锁 suǒ means lock.

sentence: 墙上有个小洞，冷风一直吹进来；爸爸用布堵住了那个洞，风不再从那里吹进来了。
grammar: 堵住 marks establishing an obstruction that blocks passage through an opening. The cloth stops air passing through the hole.
note: 洞 dòng means hole; 堵 dǔ means block or obstruct.

sentence: 盘里原来有八个饺子，弟弟吃了五个，剩下三个，正好留给晚回家的姐姐。
grammar: 剩下 predicates what remains after part of a set is removed or consumed. 下 does not describe downward movement here.

sentence: 我把豆子种在盆里，前几天只看见泥土；今天小芽长出来了，已经有两厘米高。
grammar: 出来 after 长 presents growth into visibility, rather than an existing object moving from inside to outside. The deictic syllable lai is neutral.
note: 种 zhòng means plant; 芽 yá means sprout; 泥土 nítǔ means soil; 长 is zhǎng for growth.

sentence: 我坐在桌边，姐姐从对面的书柜里拿出一本书来，递到我手里。
grammar: 来 marks movement toward the speaker. The nonplace object 一本书 separates outward-path 出 from deictic 来 in 拿出一本书来.
note: 书柜 shūguì means bookcase. The weak deictic complement is neutral-tone lai here.

sentence: 我留在门外，哥哥把那张桌子搬进屋去了，现在正往桌上放书。
grammar: 去 marks movement away from the speaker remaining outside. The place goal 屋 follows inward-path 进 and precedes deictic 去.
note: 搬 bān means move a bulky object. The weak deictic complement is neutral-tone qu here.

sentence: 我刚才说“星期天图书馆不开门”，查了通知才发现星期天也开放；我收回刚才的话，是我记错了。
grammar: 回 after 收 forms 收回, retract something already said. The statement is withdrawn rather than physically returned.
note: 收回 shōuhuí means retract or take back; 开放 kāifàng here means be open to the public.

sentence: 我今天从小安那里要回了自己的尺子；尺子是上周借给他的，现在又在我书包里了。
grammar: 要回 combines requesting an item's return with recovering it. The ruler belongs to the speaker and has actually been returned.

sentence: 我带了十二元，买笔花了四元；十二减去四等于八，正好是剩下的钱。
grammar: 减去 names subtraction, with the starting quantity before it and the subtracted quantity after it. 去 has full fourth tone in this arithmetic word.
note: 等于 děngyú means equal.

sentence: 老师问：“九减三是多少？”我想了一会儿，终于回答上来了：“六。”
grammar: 上来 after 回答 marks managing to supply the requested answer. It describes an achieved response rather than upward movement.
note: The deictic syllable lai is neutral in this complement.

sentence: 我咽下了嘴里的那小口米饭，嘴里空了，才回答妹妹的问题。
grammar: 咽下 means swallow, with 下 expressing passage downward. 咽 is yàn for swallowing, distinct from yān meaning pharynx.
note: 嘴 zuǐ means mouth; 口 kǒu counts mouthfuls.

sentence: 妈妈说：“先看说明，再装椅子。”我这次听进去了，先读完说明才开始装。
meaning: in, as advice taken to heart
grammar: 听进去 means take in and accept what someone says. Following the advice distinguishes this from merely hearing the words.
note: 说明 shuōmíng here means written instructions; 装 zhuāng here means assemble. The deictic syllable qu is neutral.

sentence: 吃晚饭时，爸爸提起去年搬家的事，妈妈接着说那次带走了哪些东西，我们聊了很久。
meaning: up, in bringing up a topic
grammar: 起 after 提 forms 提起, bring a topic into conversation. 提 has a topic-raising sense here rather than a carrying sense.

sentence: 纸上写着“八、二、五”，我看过后就闭上眼，背给妹妹听：“八、二、五。”
grammar: 背 bèi means recite from memory. It differs from carrying bēi and from reading aloud while looking at a text.
note: 闭上眼 bìshàng yǎn means close one's eyes.

sentence: 这本字典下午还要用，请把它放在我桌子的右边，别收进柜子。
meaning: marks the object placed at a stated location
grammar: 把 places the dictionary before 放在 and its resulting location. The location completes the placement instruction.
note: 柜子 guìzi means cabinet.

sentence: 这两本书是林老师要的，我已经把书交给他了，他现在拿着书看。
meaning: marks the item transferred to a recipient
grammar: 把 introduces the transferred books before 交给 and its recipient. 给 marks the recipient after the handover verb.
note: 交 jiāo means hand over; 交给 is written jiāo gěi.

sentence: 这张硬纸原来是平的，姐姐把它做成了小盒子，正好放我的两支笔。
meaning: marks material made into a resulting product
grammar: 把 introduces the starting material; 做成 introduces the product made from it. The paper and the resulting box have different roles.
note: 硬纸 yìngzhǐ means stiff paper; 盒子 hézi means box.

sentence: 弟弟把那张旧报纸撕得满地都是，我叫他自己收拾。
grammar: 得 follows 撕 and introduces the resulting situation. 满地都是 describes the torn paper scattered all over the floor.
note: 报纸 bàozhǐ means newspaper; 满地 mǎn dì means all over the floor.

sentence: 明天上课要读这段课文，我今晚把它读了两遍，第二遍比第一遍流利。
meaning: marks the object of a counted action
grammar: 读了两遍 bounds the reading by two complete passes through the text. A counted action can complete a 把 predicate without a result complement.

sentence: 昨晚屋里很热，我把窗户开了两个小时，睡觉前才关上。
meaning: marks an object kept in a state for a stated duration
grammar: 开了两个小时 states how long the window was kept open. The later closing explicitly bounds this maintained state; the duration does not measure completion of an entire task.

sentence: 这张纸太大，请把它折一折，再放进信封里。
meaning: marks a brief action between repeated verbs
grammar: 一 between repeated 折 forms the brief-action pattern 折一折. It presents a limited folding action rather than counting an object.
note: 信封 xìnfēng means envelope. In a full-tone connected realization, 一 becomes yì before second-tone zhé; it can also weaken in this pattern.

sentence: 昨晚窗户没关，风把桌上那张收据吹进了床底，今天才找到。
meaning: marks the object affected by a physical cause
grammar: The subject 风 causes the receipt's movement. A 把 clause can describe nonintentional physical causation without a human agent.
note: 吹 chuī means blow; 床底 chuángdǐ means the space beneath a bed.

sentence: 这张桌子不重，门也够宽，我一个人能把它搬进屋，不过现在还没搬。
grammar: 能 precedes 把 and expresses capacity under the stated weight and doorway conditions. The final clause says the move has not happened.

sentence: 我拿水杯时差点把电脑弄湿；杯子刚要翻倒，我就扶住了，电脑上一滴水也没有。
grammar: 差点 scopes over the whole affected-object result 把电脑弄湿. The cup was caught in time, so the computer did not become wet.
note: 翻倒 fāndǎo means overturn or tip over; 滴 dī counts drops.

sentence: 这两本书我还没寄，我打算把它们寄给姐姐，等她确认地址再去邮局。
meaning: intend to, with an affected-object action
grammar: 打算 precedes 把 and presents the following transfer as intended. The books have not yet been mailed.

sentence: 门关着，我压下把手再往里推，门就开了。
note: 把手 names the handle as a whole word, with neutral-tone shou. 压下 yāxià means press down.

sentence: 这块面包是明天的早餐，弟弟今晚把它吃了一半，剩下的一半还在盘里。
meaning: marks an object partly affected by an action
grammar: 吃了一半 specifies how much of the identified bread was eaten. 把 does not itself mean that the entire object was consumed.

sentence: 那杯水很满，我把杯子轻轻地放在桌上，水没洒出来。
meaning: links a manner expression to an action
grammar: 地 connects manner expression 轻轻 to the following placement action. This neutral de differs from noun-modifying 的 and postverbal 得.
note: 轻轻地 qīngqīng de means gently.

sentence: 老师给学生的通知写着：“请将写好的作业交给我，别放在门口。”
meaning: introduces the affected object in written instructions
grammar: 将 introduces 作业 before the handover action, functioning like 把. It is not a future-time marker here.
register: 将 suits this written notice; 把 is the usual conversational counterpart.

sentence: 这台电脑今天被弟弟摔坏了；他搬的时候没拿稳，电脑掉在地上，现在不能用了。
meaning: marks a passive event with an explicit actor
grammar: The affected computer precedes 被, and the actor 弟弟 follows it. 摔坏 reports the damage actually caused.
note: 摔坏 shuāihuài means damage through a fall or impact.

sentence: 我出门前把外套挂在门口，回来时发现它被拿走了；是谁拿的，我不知道。
meaning: marks a passive event with the actor unstated
grammar: 被 can be followed directly by the verb when the actor is unstated. The removal occurred, but the speaker does not know who performed it.

sentence: 这次作业我全写对了，被老师奖励了一本新书；我高兴地拿给妈妈看。
meaning: marks receipt of a beneficial action
grammar: 被 introduces the giver of a welcome reward. A passive can report a beneficial event and does not inherently express misfortune.

sentence: 阳台上那件外套被风吹到了楼下，邻居捡到后还给我，衣服没有破。
meaning: marks an event caused by a nonhuman force
grammar: 风 is the nonhuman causer after 被. 吹到 gives the coat's achieved destination; no deliberate human action is implied.

sentence: 搬家时，我以为那把旧椅子已经扔了；今天回去一看，它没被扔掉，还在原来的角落里。
meaning: was not, in a passive event
grammar: 没 precedes 被 to deny occurrence of the discard event. The chair remains in its former location.

sentence: 我已经提交了请假申请，经理说下午答复；现在上午十点，申请还没被批准，我等答复后再买车票。
grammar: 还没被 presents approval as not achieved by now while leaving a later decision open. It does not say approval is impossible or guaranteed.
note: 请假申请 qǐngjià shēnqǐng means a leave request; 申请 is a noun here.

sentence: 老师说，明天要把我的作文贴在教室门口；我想，这篇作文会被很多同学看到，不过现在还放在我书包里。
grammar: 会 before 被 makes a prediction based on the teacher's announced plan. 我想 identifies it as the speaker's expectation, and the display has not occurred.
note: 作文 zuòwén means a school composition.

sentence: 教室的墙正在被工人粉刷，只刷了一半；今天我们去隔壁上课。
grammar: 正在 precedes 被 to present painting as an ongoing process. Only half the wall has been painted, so the process is unfinished.
note: 粉刷 fěnshuā means paint or whitewash a wall; 隔壁 gébì means next door.

sentence: 同一份表格这周被工作人员退回了两次：第一次缺地址，第二次漏了签名；我现在补好再交。
meaning: marks the patient of counted repeated events
grammar: 两次 counts two completed returns of the same form. The form remains the patient and the staff remain the actors across both events.
note: 表格 biǎogé means form; 退回 tuìhuí means send back.

sentence: 我那句“这个办法还要再试”，被同事误解成了“我不同意”；其实我只是想先看效果。
grammar: 误解 describes assigning a mistaken meaning to the speaker's words. 成 introduces the incorrect interpretation.
note: 效果 xiàoguǒ means effect or result.

sentence: 我放在桌上的水杯让弟弟碰翻了，水洒了一地，他正拿布擦。
grammar: 让 follows the affected cup and introduces 弟弟 as the actor. It reports what happened to the cup rather than permission or an instruction.
register: 让 is a conversational alternative to 被 in this passive frame.
note: 碰翻 pèngfān means knock over by bumping into.

sentence: 我刚晒干的外套叫楼上的邻居弄湿了：他浇花时，水从上面滴下来，我只好重新晾。
grammar: 叫 introduces the neighbour as the actor affecting the coat. This passive frame uses an overt actor after 叫.
register: 叫 is conversational passive wording here, alongside 被 and passive 让.

sentence: 我放在门口的伞给人拿走了，原来的地方空着；是谁拿的，我也不知道。
grammar: 给 introduces 人 as the actor in a colloquial passive. The umbrella was taken by someone; 给 does not describe giving it to them.
register: This passive use of 给 is colloquial.

sentence: 那张刚画好的图被弟弟给撕破了，我还没拍照，只好重新画。
meaning: adds emphasis to the passive event
grammar: 给 between 被弟弟 and 撕破 adds colloquial emphasis to the event. The passive remains grammatical without 给.
register: Colloquial emphasis within an already marked 被 passive.

sentence: 经理说：“你这次做得不认真，漏了地址和签名。”我挨了批评，补好表格后重新交。
grammar: 挨 takes 批评 as the unwelcome experience received by the subject. It is a lexical verb rather than a general passive marker.
note: 批评 pīpíng means criticism here. 挨 is ái for undergoing an unwelcome action, distinct from āi for being close to something.

sentence: 林老师说：“你今天把每个字都写对了，很好！”我受了表扬，高兴地把作业拿给妈妈看。
grammar: 受 takes 表扬 as the favorable evaluation received by the subject. The verb can also occur with unwelcome experiences.
note: 表扬 biǎoyáng means praise.

sentence: 明天会议的接待工作由我负责，小安负责带客人参观；我们今天先商量具体怎么做。
grammar: 由 introduces the person responsible for the preceding task. This arrangement does not report an already completed passive event.
note: 负责 fùzé means be responsible for; 接待 jiēdài means receive or host guests.

sentence: 小安原来负责今天的接待工作，可他临时请假；我替他在门口接待了客人，他下午才回来。
meaning: in place of; as a substitute for
grammar: 替 introduces the person whose assigned role the subject takes over. It identifies substitution rather than benefit alone.
note: 临时 línshí here means at short notice.

sentence: 我在给同事的说明里写道：“桌腿下新加的木块使桌面高了五厘米，原来的椅子现在太矮了。”
grammar: 使 links the cause 木块 to the affected subject 桌面 and its resulting increase in height.
register: 使 suits this written explanation; 让 is often the more conversational causative choice.
note: 写道 xiědào introduces quoted written words.

sentence: 给客人的留言上写着：“我们为您准备了茶和水果，请先在这里休息，房间马上就好。”
grammar: 为 introduces the guest benefiting from the preparations. It is read wèi in this function.
register: 为 suits this written welcome; conversational 给 can also introduce a beneficiary.
note: 留言 liúyán means a message left for someone.

sentence: 图书馆的牌子离这里只有两米，灯也够亮；不用走近，在这儿就看得见上面的字。
grammar: 看得见 expresses visual access under the stated distance and lighting conditions. It does not narrate a completed act of noticing.
note: 牌子 páizi means sign.

sentence: 这张通知上的字很大，我都认识，可它只写着“按原方案办理”，没说是什么方案，我看不懂，得问老师。
grammar: 看不懂 concerns unavailable comprehension of the written message. The characters themselves are visible and recognizable.
note: 原 yuán means original or previously established; 方案 fāng'àn means plan; 办理 bànlǐ means handle a procedure.

sentence: 隔壁正在敲墙，我能听见你在说话，可听不清每个字；请你发短信告诉我见面地点。
grammar: 听不清 expresses a present obstacle to clear auditory perception. Sound is audible, but individual words are unclear.

sentence: 姐姐教我用一只手系鞋带，我试了十几次还是学不会；换成两只手，我已经会系了。
grammar: 学不会 concerns inability to acquire this particular technique through the attempts described. It does not claim permanent inability to learn.
note: 系鞋带 jì xiédài means tie shoelaces.

sentence: 新门锁的密码是四七二九，姐姐说了三遍，我还是记不住，刚听完就把顺序弄混了；请写下来给我吧。
grammar: 记不住 expresses difficulty retaining newly supplied information. The number is lost immediately after hearing it.
note: 门锁 ménsuǒ means door lock; 弄混 nònghùn means mix up.

sentence: 以前我每天去那家面馆，店名一直记得很清楚；姐姐现在问我叫什么，我却想不起来，只记得最后一个字是“家”。
grammar: 想不起来 expresses inability to retrieve something previously known. The weak final syllable lai is neutral.
note: 面馆 miànguǎn means noodle restaurant; 店名 diànmíng means shop name.

sentence: 我们想在小教室里同时放六张桌子，又要留出走路的地方；商量了半天，我还是想不出来该怎么摆，想请老师帮忙。
meaning: cannot devise; cannot think of a solution
grammar: 想不出来 concerns producing a new solution through thought, rather than recalling a solution already known. The final lai is neutral.
note: 留出 liúchū means leave available; 摆 bǎi means position or arrange.

sentence: 这袋米有三十公斤，我用双手试了两次，袋子一点也没离地；我拿不动，得请哥哥一起抬。
meaning: cannot lift or move by carrying
grammar: 拿不动 expresses insufficient strength to move the load. 动 is the movement result that cannot be achieved.
note: 双手 shuāngshǒu means both hands; 抬 tái here means lift or carry together.

sentence: 离下班只剩十分钟，我还有二十份表格没核对，每份要两分钟；今天肯定做不完，我得告诉经理，把剩下的留到明早。
grammar: 做不完 expresses inability to complete the bounded workload within the available time. It does not merely report noncompletion.
note: 肯定 kěndìng here means certainly.

sentence: “这六本书还在桌上，你确定这个包装得下吗？”“我昨天用同样大小的六本书试过，拉链也能拉上。”
grammar: 装得下 asks whether the container has sufficient capacity for the books. The current books have not yet been packed.
note: 拉链 lāliàn means zipper.

sentence: “再吃一个包子吧。”“谢谢，我刚吃了两碗面，已经饱了，实在吃不下了，留给别人吧。”
grammar: 吃不下 expresses inability to take more food because the eater is full. Final 了 marks the current changed limit.
note: 实在 shízài here means really or simply, emphasizing the stated limit.

sentence: 店里这台电脑还没卖，价格是六千元；我手里只有三千元，又不想借钱，现在买不起，只好以后再说。
grammar: 买不起 expresses an affordability limit. The computer is available, but its price exceeds the speaker's funds.

sentence: 那场演出的票每张五十元，我带了一百元来，可窗口已经贴出“全部售完”，现在买不到，只好等下次。
grammar: 买不到 expresses unavailable purchase attainment. The speaker has enough money, but the tickets are sold out.
note: 窗口 chuāngkǒu here means ticket window; 全部售完 quánbù shòuwán means all sold out.

sentence: 现在两点，图书馆三点关门，走过去只要十分钟；我们还来得及借书，这就走吧。
grammar: 来得及 expresses sufficient time to perform the following action before the relevant deadline. 来 is full-tone lái in this expression.

sentence: “你怎么不去打印店了？”“店主说五点关门，现在四点五十五分，走到那里要二十分钟，来不及了；我明早再去。”
grammar: 来不及 expresses insufficient time to reach the shop before closing. The second syllable bu is neutral in this lexicalized expression.
note: 店主 diànzhǔ means shop owner.

sentence: 隔壁一直大声放音乐，我实在受不了，想先去院子里待一会儿，等安静些再回来。
grammar: 受不了 expresses inability to tolerate the continuing noise. 了 is liǎo in this potential expression, rather than aspectual le.
note: 待 dāi means stay here; 放音乐 fàng yīnyuè means play music.

sentence: 爸爸把帽子戴反了，问我好不好看；我想忍着不笑，可还是忍不住，笑出了声。
grammar: 忍不住 expresses inability to suppress an impulse. The attempted restraint and ensuing laughter are both explicit.
note: 忍 rěn means endure or hold back; 戴反 dàifǎn means put on back to front.

sentence: “这间客房外面就是大路，你晚上能休息吗？”“关好窗户就很安静，我睡得着，你放心吧。”
grammar: 睡得着 expresses the possibility of attaining sleep under the stated conditions. 着 is resultative zháo, not durative zhe.
note: 客房 kèfáng means guest room.

sentence: 书柜最上层那本字典比我举起的手还高，我够不着；姐姐，请帮我拿下来。
grammar: 够不着 expresses inability to reach the dictionary physically. 够 means reach here, and 着 is attainment-result zháo.

sentence: 我站在院门外，门虽然只开了一半，空隙还是比我肩膀宽；弟弟问要不要再推开，我说：“不用，我走得进去。”
meaning: can walk in, away from the speaker's present position
grammar: 得 precedes 进去 to express an achievable inward path. 去 points away from the speaker's current position outside and has neutral qu.
note: 空隙 kòngxì means gap; 肩膀 jiānbǎng means shoulder.

sentence: 我在教室门外等妹妹，门口堆满了刚搬来的椅子，她从里面出不来；我挪开几把，她才走到我旁边。
grammar: 出不来 expresses a blocked outward path toward the speaker waiting outside. 来 is the weak neutral-tone deictic component.
note: 堆 duī means pile or heap.

sentence: 我和同事都还在公司；他家在河对面，唯一的桥今天临时关闭，他一时回不去，只好留在这里，等桥重新开放。
grammar: 回不去 expresses temporarily unavailable return to an established place away from the present speaker location. 去 is neutral qu here.
note: 唯一 wéiyī means the only one; 桥 qiáo means bridge; 一时 yīshí here means for the moment.

sentence: “现在七点四十，八点的公交车还没发车，走到车站要十分钟，我们赶得上吗？”“时间够，收好东西现在走吧。”
grammar: 赶得上 asks whether timely arrival for the scheduled service is achievable. It does not report already catching or boarding it.
note: 发车 fāchē means depart, of a vehicle.

sentence: 我把家里的抽屉都翻过了，连书包也倒空看了，还是找不到那把钥匙；你记得我最后一次用它是什么时候吗？
grammar: 找不到 expresses inability to locate the key despite the search described. The key has not been recovered.

sentence: 这是林老师二十年前和同学的合照；每张脸都很清楚，可我认不出哪位是现在教我的林老师，请你指给我看。
grammar: 认不出 concerns unavailable identity recognition despite clear visual access. 出 marks the identification result that cannot be attained.
note: 合照 hézhào means group photograph; 指 zhǐ here means point out.

sentence: 这两把钥匙大小和颜色都一样，也没有不同的标记；我分不清哪把开家门、哪把开办公室门，得一把一把试。
grammar: 分不清 expresses inability to distinguish the two keys by their appearance. It concerns discrimination rather than auditory clarity.
note: 标记 biāojì means identifying mark.

sentence: 这台旧钟里断了一个零件，我没有新的零件，拆开检查过也修不好；得请修理店的人看看。
grammar: 修不好 expresses inability to restore working condition with the available means. Inspecting the clock does not itself achieve repair.
note: 钟 zhōng means clock; 零件 língjiàn means component or spare part.

sentence: 白衬衫上那块墨水印，我用手洗了三遍，怎么搓都洗不干净；今天先换另一件穿吧。
grammar: 不 precedes the complete result adjective 干净. The washing attempted here cannot achieve removal of this particular stain.
note: 墨水 mòshuǐ means ink; 印 yìn here means mark or stain.

sentence: 这把椅子是你自己装好的，先做什么、后做什么，你说得清楚吗？我还没动手，想先听你讲一遍。
grammar: 说得清楚 asks whether the listener can give a clear explanation. The firsthand assembly experience supports this prospective ability question.
note: 动手 dòngshǒu here means begin doing the practical work.

sentence: “如果我用中文说‘先洗手，再吃饭’，你听得懂吗？”“懂，就是吃饭以前要先洗手；你可以继续用中文说。”
grammar: 听得懂 asks about comprehension available through listening. The reply demonstrates understanding by restating the instruction.
note: 继续 jìxù means continue.

sentence: 我们原来打算用教室的电脑做表格，可突然停电了，这项工作现在做不了；先在纸上写好内容，等有电了再做。
grammar: 做不了 expresses situational inability to carry out the computer-based task. 了 is liǎo here, not aspectual le.
note: 项 xiàng counts tasks or projects.

sentence: 这瓶水的盖子有点紧，我试着转了一下，已经松动了；我开得开，你不用帮忙，先把杯子拿来吧。
grammar: The first 开 names the opening action; the second 开 specifies its achievable open result. The cap has loosened but has not yet been removed.
note: 松动 sōngdòng means become loose; 转 is zhuàn for rotating the cap.

sentence: 门口横着一把椅子，挡住了门，门一直关不上；我先把椅子挪开，再关门。
grammar: 关不上 expresses inability to attain closure because an object obstructs the door. It does not concern securing a lock.
note: 挡住 dǎngzhù means block or obstruct.

sentence: 我想把姐姐家的旧桌子带回家，桌子不重，可今天我骑的是自行车，没法装这么大的东西；今天带不走，只好下次开大车来拿。
grammar: 带不走 expresses inability to remove the table from the sister's home using the available transport. Its weight is not the obstacle.
note: 没法 méi fǎ means have no way to.

sentence: 妈妈今天第一次一个人换乘地铁来找我，我心里放不下，先给她打电话，确认她到了哪一站，才继续工作。
grammar: 放不下 expresses continuing concern about the mother's unfamiliar journey. It does not describe insufficient physical space.

sentence: 拍合照前，姐姐指着旁边的一小块空地问：“这里地面平，也不滑，你站得住吗？我们要站着拍一分钟。”“没问题，我不用扶东西。”
grammar: 住 specifies maintained physical stability after 站. 得 presents that stability as achievable during the proposed photograph.
note: 空地 kòngdì means open space; 地面 dìmiàn means ground surface.

sentence: 这个布袋我昨天装了三公斤书，来回提了十几次，袋底和提手都没坏；它经得起这样的反复提拿，明天带同样多的书就用它。
grammar: 经得起 takes the particular demand or test that something can withstand. The claim here is limited to repeated carrying of the stated load.
note: 布袋 bùdài means cloth bag; 提手 tíshǒu means carrying handle; 反复 fǎnfù means repeatedly.

sentence: “明天要量教室的宽度，我这把五米长的卷尺用得上吗？”“正好，教室不到五米宽，请带来吧。”
meaning: can be useful for the need
grammar: 用得上 expresses an available use for an item in a particular situation. It does not say that the item is already being used.
note: 宽度 kuāndù means width; 卷尺 juǎnchǐ means tape measure.

sentence: 客人已经到了，我正忙着给大家倒茶，顾不上接电话；姐姐，请你替我接一下，问问是谁。
grammar: 顾不上 introduces something that competing demands prevent someone from attending to. Serving the guests takes priority over answering the phone here.
note: 接电话 jiē diànhuà means answer the phone. 不 retains lexical bù in this transcription.

sentence: 报名桌前一下来了六个人，有人问上课时间，有人交表格，还有人要改电话号码；我一个人忙不过来，请旁边的同事先帮忙回答问题。
meaning: cannot cope with all the work
grammar: 忙不过来 expresses insufficient capacity to deal with the demands arriving at once. 过来 has an extended coping meaning, with neutral lai.
note: 报名桌 bàomíng zhuō means registration desk; 一下 yīxià here means all at once.

sentence: “周三下午三点到四点再加一次排练，行吗？”“那天下午两点到四点上课，四点到六点接待客人，时间实在排不开；改到周四上午吧。”
grammar: 排不开 describes insufficient room in a schedule for another arrangement. 排 concerns arranging time here, rather than forming a queue.
note: 排练 páiliàn means rehearse; 加 jiā here means add an activity to the schedule.

sentence: 我和新同事午休时常一起聊天，喜欢的话题很多，意见不同时也愿意听对方解释；我们挺合得来，周末还约着一起看电影。
grammar: 合得来 describes interpersonal compatibility. 来 retains full-tone lái in this metaphorical expression.
note: 午休 wǔxiū means midday break; 话题 huàtí means topic of conversation; 对方 duìfāng means the other person.

sentence: 我想把合租房的打扫时间定在周六早上，室友那时上班，只能周日来；可我周日全天有课，我们商量了很久还是谈不拢，只好先各自打扫自己的房间。
grammar: 拢 after 谈 concerns convergence on an agreement. 谈不拢 reports that discussion cannot resolve the incompatible proposals described.
note: 合租房 hézūfáng means shared rented accommodation; 室友 shìyǒu means roommate.

sentence: 弟弟说：“他只是个送货的，懂什么？”我说：“别因为别人的工作看不起人；他刚才帮我们找出了地址上的错误。”
grammar: 看不起 is a lexical expression of contempt. It does not refer to poor vision or lack of money.
note: 送货 sòng huò means deliver goods. The middle syllable bu is neutral in kànbuqǐ.

sentence: 这家店的外套都在我的预算内，可我一件也看不上：我要有口袋的，这里的都没有；我们去另一家看看吧。
grammar: 看不上 expresses that the available options do not meet the speaker's requirements. The explicit budget rules out unaffordability as the issue.
note: 预算 yùsuàn means budget; 口袋 kǒudài means pocket. The middle bu is neutral in this selected lexical reading.

sentence: 老师让我独立安排一次小组活动；我定好时间、借好教室，还通知了每个人。老师说：“你有组织活动的能力，下次也可以试着负责。”
grammar: 能力 is a noun for capacity to perform a task. 组织活动的 specifies the particular capacity being evaluated.
note: 独立 dúlì means independently; 小组 xiǎozǔ means small group; 组织 zǔzhī means organize here.

sentence: 这把旧椅子的腿总晃，我照着说明换好零件，又把松的地方拧紧，终于修好了；爸爸坐着试过，笑着说：“你还真有本事！”
grammar: 有本事 praises practical skill in handling a task. The comment refers to the successful repair just described.
register: 本事 is conversational wording for practical skill; the father's comment is appreciative here.
note: The second syllable shi is neutral in this skill sense.

sentence: 活动室的老师说：“今天每组最多借两把椅子。”因为这项数量限制，我们借了两把，又从自己教室搬来两把，凑够四把。
grammar: 限制 is the noun for a constraint on what is allowed. 数量 identifies the constrained dimension, and 两把 gives its actual limit.
note: 活动室 huódòngshì means activity room; 数量 shùliàng means quantity; 凑够 còugòu means assemble enough.

sentence: 读书小组的通知写着：“参加满三次活动的成员可以报名主持下次讨论。”我已经参加了四次，有报名资格，但还没决定要不要报名。
grammar: 资格 denotes eligibility under the group's stated criterion. Meeting that criterion does not itself establish skill or a decision to participate.
note: 成员 chéngyuán means member; 主持 zhǔchí means lead or chair an activity.

sentence: 我想借用教室拍小组照片，先问了负责教室的老师；他答应让我们下午三点使用，我得到他的许可后，才通知大家过来。
grammar: 许可 is a noun after 得到, referring to permission granted by the teacher responsible for the room.
note: 借用 jièyòng means borrow for use; 使用 shǐyòng means use.

sentence: 活动室刚铺好地毯，管理员贴出通知：“今天禁止把饮料带进室内。”这条临时禁令只适用于今天，大家把水杯留在门外再进去。
grammar: 禁令 names the prohibitory instruction issued by the administrator. Its scope is explicitly limited to this room and this day.
register: 禁令 is formal wording for a prohibitory order, appropriate to discussing the posted instruction.
note: 地毯 dìtǎn means carpet; 管理员 guǎnlǐyuán means administrator or attendant; 适用 shìyòng means apply to.

sentence: 我在给老师的活动报告里写道：“昨天借来的投影仪突然坏了，我们未能按计划播放短片，后来改为展示照片。”
grammar: 未能 reports failure to achieve the planned action on the stated occasion. It does not claim lasting inability.
register: 未能 suits this written report; 没能 is a common conversational counterpart.
note: 报告 bàogào means report; 投影仪 tóuyǐngyí means projector; 短片 duǎnpiàn means short film; 展示 zhǎnshì means display.

sentence: “昨天怎么没来听我的演唱？”“我本来很想来，也已经出门了，可公交车半路坏了，我没能在开始前赶到；真抱歉。”
grammar: 没能 presents the desired arrival as unachieved because of the past transport problem. It concerns that occasion, rather than a present prohibition.
register: 没能 is natural in this conversational explanation; 未能 also expresses nonachievement in written reports.
note: 演唱 yǎnchàng means vocal performance here; 半路 bànlù means midway on a journey; 赶到 gǎndào means get somewhere in time or after hurrying.

sentence: 我们原来没有地方排练，我去问了活动室的老师，终于把借教室的事办成了；老师已经确认，明天下午两点到四点可以用。
grammar: 办成 combines handling a practical matter with its successful accomplishment. 成 concerns success here, rather than transformation into a material or shape.
note: 借教室的事 jiè jiàoshì de shì means the matter of borrowing a classroom.

sentence: 读书小组的负责人说：“借书卡补办要先核对姓名和照片；你今天没带照片，这件事现在办不了，明天带来再办吧。”
grammar: 办不了 expresses that the stated procedure cannot be carried out under the present conditions. 了 is liǎo, not aspectual le.
note: 借书卡 jièshūkǎ means library borrowing card; 补办 bǔbàn means arrange a replacement through the relevant procedure. The requirement belongs to this reading group.

sentence: 我们三个人按小安、我、姐姐的顺序介绍自己的照片；小安刚讲完，现在轮到我了，我先把照片递给大家看。
grammar: 轮到 takes the participant whose turn has arrived. The preceding list establishes the order and the completed first turn.

sentence: 这次读书会由我担任主持人；活动开始时，我先介绍讨论顺序，再请大家轮流说自己的看法。
grammar: 担任 takes a role noun, 主持人. It identifies the position the speaker fills, with the following actions illustrating its duties.
note: 读书会 dúshūhuì means reading-group meeting; 主持人 zhǔchírén means host or discussion chair; 看法 kànfǎ means view or opinion.

sentence: 原来我一个人付整套房子的房租，每月四千元，对我来说负担太重；现在和朋友合租，每人付两千，月底终于能剩下一点钱。
grammar: 负担 is a noun for the load borne by someone. 太重 evaluates the rent burden, while the amounts identify its size and later reduction.
note: 整套 zhěng tào means the whole unit here; 合租 hézū means share rented accommodation.

sentence: 我们约好一起办生日聚会：姐姐负责做饭，我承担买饮料的费用；饮料一共八十元，我已经付了，没再向大家收钱。
grammar: 承担 takes the cost that the subject agrees to bear. The payment and absence of collection from others establish who actually pays.
note: 聚会 jùhuì means gathering or party; 费用 fèiyòng means expense or cost.

sentence: 出差前，我给同事留了书面说明：“我委托你在周五替我领取这批书，领到后交给图书室的王老师；他会在门口等你。”
grammar: 委托 takes the entrusted person followed by the task. The speaker delegates collection and onward handover of the books.
register: 委托 suits this written delegation; 托 is a shorter conversational alternative.
note: 书面 shūmiàn means written; 批 pī counts a batch; 图书室 túshūshì means a book room or small library.

sentence: 妈妈把一包茶寄给我，请我转送给住在附近的外婆；我今天把茶带到外婆家，告诉她是妈妈送的。
meaning: pass on something sent by another person
grammar: 转送 describes onward delivery through an intermediary. The mother is the sender, the speaker carries the tea onward, and the grandmother is the final recipient.
note: 转 is zhuǎn in this onward-transfer compound, distinct from spinning zhuàn.

sentence: 老师把活动室钥匙交给我时，交代了两件事：“最后一个人离开时要关窗、锁门，钥匙明早还给我。”我当场记在本子上。
meaning: give instructions; explain what must be done
grammar: 交代 introduces instructions given when responsibility is handed over. The quotation states both the required actions and the key's return time.
note: 当场 dāngchǎng means on the spot, at that time and place.

sentence: 搬家前，我和姐姐商量好了：那把旧椅子归我，她拿新椅子；今天我先把旧椅子搬进了自己的房间。
grammar: 归 takes the person to whom an item belongs or is allotted. Here it predicates the agreed ownership of the old chair.

sentence: 两个小组都以为这台打印机是自己的；老师拿出购买记录，确认它是摄影组买的，才弄清了打印机的归属，并在机器上贴好组名。
grammar: 归属 is a noun naming the relation of belonging. The purchase record identifies the group that owns this printer.
note: 购买 gòumǎi means purchase; 摄影组 shèyǐng zǔ means photography group; 组名 zǔmíng means group name.

sentence: 我要出差三天，花店老板答应每天替我浇花；我把两盆花交给他托管，周五回来再去取，费用也已经说好了。
meaning: entrust to another's care or management
grammar: 托管 describes placing something under another person's entrusted care. The arrangement specifies the caretaker, daily task, duration and later collection.
note: 花店 huādiàn means flower shop.

sentence: 姐姐原来负责核对报名表，今天核对到第十二份就要去上课；我从第十三份开始接手，把剩下八份核对完，再把结果告诉她。
grammar: 接手 means become the person handling work previously handled by someone else. The thirteenth form marks the precise handover point.
note: 报名表 bàomíngbiǎo means registration form.

sentence: 相框里的旧照片已经褪色，我用上周拍的新合照替换了它；旧照片收进相册，相框里现在是大家的新照片。
grammar: 用 A 替换 B identifies A as the replacement and B as the item removed. The old photograph is retained elsewhere rather than discarded.
note: 褪色 tuìsè means fade in colour; 相册 xiàngcè means photograph album.

sentence: 客人不小心把汤洒在桌上，服务员马上处理了这个问题：先请客人换到旁边的桌子，再擦干桌面，换上干净的桌布。
grammar: 处理 takes the concrete problem being dealt with. The following actions specify what handling it involved.
note: 桌布 zhuōbù means tablecloth. 处 is chǔ in 处理, distinct from chù in place-related words.

sentence: 我在活动室的清理记录里写道：“旧桌椅已按原定办法处置：能修的送去修理，不能修的送去回收，门口现在已经清空。”
meaning: dispose of; decide and carry out what is done with
grammar: 处置 concerns what is done with the affected items. The report states the different destinations of repairable and irreparable furniture.
register: 处置 suits this written account of how old items were dealt with; 处理 is a broader everyday alternative.
note: 清理 qīnglǐ means clear out or sort out; 原定 yuándìng means previously decided; 回收 huíshōu means collect for recycling; 清空 qīngkōng means empty or clear.

sentence: 搬家后，我发现台灯的底座受损，裂了一道口子，放在平整的桌面上也站不稳；是谁搬的时候碰的，我还不知道。
grammar: 受损 predicates damage to the lamp base without naming an actor. The crack and loss of stability describe the actual damage.
note: 台灯 táidēng means desk lamp; 底座 dǐzuò means base; 裂 liè means split or crack; 口子 kǒuzi here means a split or opening. 平整 píngzhěng means even or level.

sentence: 弟弟搬椅子时撞倒了台灯，损坏了开关；原来一按就亮的灯，现在怎么按都不亮了，他答应拿去修。
grammar: 损坏 is transitive here, with 弟弟 as the actor and 开关 as the affected component. The lamp's changed response establishes loss of function.
note: 开关 kāiguān means switch.

sentence: 我花六十元买了六个杯子，搬家时摔碎两个；这二十元的损失我自己承担，不让帮忙搬家的朋友赔。
grammar: 损失 is a noun quantified by 二十元. It names the value lost through the two broken cups, rather than the cups' damaged condition.

sentence: 我在整理记录里写道：“这张旧地图原来破成两半，今天已经修复，两半接好了，可以重新挂起来。”
grammar: 修复 names restoration of a damaged object. The two halves have been joined, making the map usable for display again.
register: 修复 suits this written restoration record and can also be used in speech about damaged objects.
note: 接 jiē here means join or connect separate parts.

sentence: 这台旧录音机以前能播放，也能录音，后来录音功能坏了，只能播放；换好零件以后，师傅恢复了它的录音功能，现在又能录下声音了。
grammar: 恢复 takes 录音功能 as the lost capability being restored. This is a transitive restoration frame, rather than resuming attendance at an interrupted activity.
note: 录音机 lùyīnjī means audio recorder; 师傅 shīfu here means a skilled repair worker; 功能 gōngnéng means function or capability; 录 lù means record sound here.

sentence: 我的水杯翻倒后，水流进打印机，造成了故障；刚才还能打印的机器，现在不动了，桌上的文件只打印了一半。
grammar: 造成 takes the resulting fault as its object. The preceding water spill supplies the cause, and the stopped printing supplies observable consequences.
note: 故障 gùzhàng means fault or malfunction; 文件 wénjiàn means document.

sentence: 我把活动开始时间从三点改成四点，却忘了通知大家，导致两位同学三点就到了，在门口等了一个小时。
grammar: 导致 introduces the consequence of changing the time without notifying everyone. Here its complement is a clause describing the classmates' early arrival and wait.

sentence: 明天搬家，我打算用软纸把杯子包好，避免路上碰坏；纸还没找齐，我现在先去找。
grammar: 避免 introduces the unwanted outcome the planned wrapping is intended to prevent. Neither the wrapping nor its preventive result has occurred yet.
note: 包 bāo means wrap here; 软纸 ruǎn zhǐ means soft paper.

sentence: 昨天下午我有两个小时可以填表，却一直拖延，先聊天再看照片；直到晚上要交了才动手，结果漏了地址。
grammar: 拖延 describes putting off the task despite having time available. The speaker chooses other activities before finally starting.
note: 填表 tián biǎo means fill in a form.

sentence: 我正在核对表格，弟弟一直在旁边问问题，妨碍了我工作；我还是核对完了，只是比平时多花了十分钟。
grammar: 妨碍 takes 我工作 as the activity being hindered. The work is completed, but the interruption makes it take longer.
note: 平时 píngshí means at ordinary times; usually.

sentence: 弟弟要扔掉那张名单，我按住他的手，阻止他把纸扔进垃圾桶；名单现在收在抽屉里，上面的电话号码还要核对。
grammar: 阻止 takes the person stopped, 他, followed by the action prevented. The intervention and retained list establish that the discard was prevented.
note: 垃圾桶 lājītǒng means rubbish bin.

sentence: 我在给同事的留言里写道：“你所提交的表格已经收到，我核对以后再答复。”
meaning: marks the object relation in a written modifier
grammar: 所 precedes transitive 提交 in 你所提交的表格. 表格 is the item submitted by 你; 的 still connects the modifier to its noun.
register: 所 is common in written identifying phrases; conversation often uses 你提交的表格.

sentence: 姐姐昨天寄给我两本书；她寄给我的那本字典放在桌上，另一本故事书还在包里。
meaning: links a transfer clause to the transferred item
grammar: 她寄给我的 identifies 字典. 她 is the sender, 我 is the recipient, and 字典 supplies the item mailed.
note: 故事书 gùshìshū means storybook.

sentence: 昨天我们在二楼开会；我们开会的那间教室今天锁着，请去一楼找林老师。
meaning: links an event clause to its place
grammar: 我们开会的 modifies 教室 by identifying where the meeting took place. 教室 is the event's location, rather than an object of 开会.
note: 开会 kāihuì means hold or attend a meeting.

sentence: 上周六我们搬家；搬家的那天也是姐姐生日，晚上收拾完才一起吃了蛋糕。
meaning: links an event clause to its day
grammar: 搬家的 identifies 那天 by the event occurring on that day. The noun head supplies a temporal relation, rather than a participant or place.
note: 蛋糕 dàngāo means cake.

sentence: 《回家》是这学期小组一起读过的三本书之一；另外两本是《小院》和《新邻居》。
grammar: 之一 follows the noun phrase naming the three-book set and selects one member. It does not mean first in an order.
note: 学期 xuéqī means school term; 《 》 enclose titles.

sentence: 我准备把这把用来量长度的卷尺借给姐姐；她明天要量书柜，现在还没拿走。
grammar: 用来量长度的 identifies 卷尺 by its function. 用来 introduces the intended use without asserting that this measuring action has already occurred.
note: 长度 chángdù means length.

sentence: 姐姐发来短信：“明天图书馆不开门。”我刚收到图书馆明天不开门的消息，还没向工作人员核实，先别急着改计划。
meaning: links reported content to a news noun
grammar: 图书馆明天不开门 gives the content of 消息. 消息 does not fill a missing argument in that clause. The report comes from the sister and remains unchecked.
note: 核实 héshí means verify; 工作人员 gōngzuò rényuán means staff.

sentence: 我用“小林”这个名字写了一本叫《门口的小猫》的书；你昨天借走的那本书的作者就是我。
grammar: 作者 names the person who wrote the book. 你昨天借走的那本书 first identifies the book whose author is being identified.

sentence: 姐姐借给我两本书；我昨晚读完的那本书的封面上画着一棵树，另一本上画着猫，你帮我拿画树那本吧。
grammar: 封面 names the book's outer cover. The completed reading identifies the book, and the tree on its cover helps the listener select it.

sentence: 我借来的那本做饭小册子，目录上写着“第一节：煮饭，第二节：拌菜”；我想学拌菜，就直接翻到第二节。
grammar: 目录 lists section titles and their order. The second listed section directs the reader to the vegetable-mixing instructions.
note: 小册子 xiǎocèzi means booklet; 拌菜 bàn cài means mix a vegetable dish.

sentence: 老师发来十张活动照片；我负责整理的部分只有三张，另外七张由姐姐整理。
grammar: 部分 refers to the speaker's three-photo subset of the ten. 我负责整理的 identifies which portion is meant.

sentence: 这本讲种花的书一共十章，我只读了两章；姐姐把整本书都读完了，最后一章讲什么她也记得。
grammar: 整 precedes classifier 本 and extends the reference to the whole book. The ten-chapter total contrasts with the speaker's two chapters.
note: 章 zhāng counts chapters.

sentence: “照片里那把椅子是去年修好的吗？”“对，你现在坐的就是同一把，椅背上还留着当时写的日期。”
grammar: 同一 asserts that the photographed chair and the chair now being used are one object. In 同一把, 把 is the classifier and 椅子 is omitted because the chair is already identified.
note: 椅背 yǐbèi means the back of a chair.

sentence: 柜子里有两只杯子，一只写着“小安”，一只没有字；写着名字的那只已经洗好，我再洗另一只，等会儿给你用。
grammar: 另一 precedes classifier 只 and selects a distinct member from the one already identified. In this two-cup set, it means the other cup.

sentence: 这三间教室中，两间正在上课；左边那间是唯一空着的教室，我们先问老师能不能借来排练。
grammar: 唯一 restricts the qualifying classroom to one within the stated three-room set. Being empty does not itself establish permission to borrow it.

sentence: 摄影组借二楼教室，读书组借一楼教室；请各组负责借教室的人把楼层写在表格上，别只写组名。
grammar: 各 modifies 组 and distributes the instruction across the two groups. Each group's responsible person records that group's floor.
note: 楼层 lóucéng means floor or storey of a building.

sentence: 桌上这三本已经登记好的书，你可以借走任何一本，不用照左边到右边的顺序拿；一次只借一本就行。
grammar: 任何 permits free selection of one member from the three registered books. The one-book limit remains in force; the listener need not take all three.

sentence: 今天要搬走的椅子一共六把，所有椅子都要贴上“小组活动”四个字，一把也别漏；门边那两把也在这六把里面。
grammar: 所有 covers every chair in the identified six-chair set. 都 reinforces the instruction's application to the complete set, including the two by the door.

sentence: 我在小组留言里写：“某位成员借走了红封面的书，还没还；我知道是谁，但不想让全组都知道姓名，请本人今天联系我。”
grammar: 某 refers to a particular member without revealing the person's identity to the group. The writer explicitly knows who the member is.
note: 本人 běnrén means the person concerned here; 姓名 xìngmíng means full name.

sentence: 我请同事把明天活动的相关信息发给我，特别是开始时间和教室位置；去年的照片这次先不用发。
grammar: 相关 modifies 信息 and connects it to tomorrow's activity. The request specifies timing and room location as the details needed.
note: 位置 wèizhi means position or location.

sentence: 老师把有关明天参观的通知发给家长，里面只写了集合时间和地点，没写午饭安排；我准备再问问。
grammar: 有关 introduces 明天参观 within the noun modifier 有关明天参观的通知. It identifies the matter the notice concerns.
note: 家长 jiāzhǎng means a child's parent or guardian; 集合 jíhé means assemble.

sentence: 老师在活动通知里写道：“画画所需的材料只有纸和彩笔，请每组带两张纸、一盒彩笔，其他东西不用带。”
grammar: 所需 combines 所 with 需, need, to identify the materials required for drawing. 材料 is the overt head, and 画画 identifies the activity requiring them.
register: 所需 is compact written wording suited to this materials notice.
note: 材料 cáiliào means materials; 彩笔 cǎibǐ means coloured pen.

sentence: 姐姐刚才说：“三点在车站门口见。”我把她所说的记在本子上，时间和地点都写清楚了。
grammar: 所说 combines with following 的 to form 她所说的, what she said. The preceding quotation supplies the actual content, and 她 identifies its speaker.

sentence: 我在给新同事的介绍里写道：“曾负责接待工作的林老师，现在教中文；他熟悉这间活动室，有问题可以先问他。”
grammar: 曾 places the reception responsibility in a former period within the modifier identifying Teacher Lin. It is a shorter form alongside 曾经, not a tense ending.
register: 曾 is concise written wording suited to this introduction.
note: 熟悉 shúxī means be familiar with.

sentence: 那把椅子原来一坐就摇晃，换了零件也没稳下来；我在记录里写：“仍在摇晃的那把椅子先别用，下午再修。”
grammar: 仍 marks continuation of the wobbling despite replacement of a component. The continuing state identifies the chair in the written instruction.
register: 仍 is a concise written alternative to 仍然 or 还 in this continuation sense.

sentence: 我刚刚收到的那包书还没拆开，就放在门边；昨天收到的那包已经收进书柜，别拿错了。
grammar: 刚刚 places receipt very shortly before speaking. The recent completed event identifies one package, contrasting with the package received yesterday.

sentence: 老师发来的活动记录写着：“十份申请中，八份已经批准，尚未批准的两份申请明早才有答复，请申请人先别买车票。”
grammar: 尚未 marks approval as unachieved by the current reference time. The two pending applications are identified, but their eventual approval is not promised.
register: 尚未 suits this written status record; 还没 is a common conversational counterpart.
note: 申请人 shēnqǐngrén means applicant.

sentence: 现在四点五十分，五点开会；老师在通知里写道：“即将开始的会议在二楼教室，请大家现在过去。”
grammar: 即将 marks the scheduled start as imminent within the modifier identifying the meeting. The stated times establish a ten-minute interval.
register: 即将 suits this written announcement; 快要 is common in conversation.

sentence: 活动室原来有四把椅子，今天又买了两把；原有的四把椅子都贴着红纸，新买的两把还没贴，一共六把。
grammar: 原有 identifies the four chairs present before the two additions. It concerns membership in the earlier inventory rather than the chairs' age or condition.

sentence: 活动室现有的六把椅子下午都要用；我们计划下周再买两把，但今天还是只能坐六个人。
grammar: 现有 identifies the current six-chair inventory. The two planned purchases are excluded from today's available seating.

sentence: 我把画画课要用的各类材料分开放：纸放左边，彩笔放右边；同一类都放在一起，方便大家拿。
meaning: different kinds of; the various types of
grammar: 各 distributes across 类, kinds. The materials are grouped by category, here paper and coloured pens, rather than by individual piece.
note: 分开放 fēnkāi fàng means put in separate places.

sentence: 借书桌上有两本教种花的书，一本讲阳台，一本讲院子；这两本同类书内容不完全相同，你可以先看目录再选。
grammar: 同类 marks a shared category: both distinct books concern growing flowers. It does not identify them as one object or assert identical content.
note: 完全 wánquán means completely.

sentence: 小安加入了摄影组，姐姐加入了读书组；老师请他们在报名表上写出自己所属的小组，小安写“摄影组”，姐姐写“读书组”。
grammar: 自己所属的小组 identifies the group each participant belongs to. The relation is group membership, rather than ownership of an object.
note: 加入 jiārù means join a group or organization.

sentence: 通知写着：“读书组用红卡，摄影组用蓝卡。”请大家拿相应颜色的卡，别只按自己喜欢的颜色选。
grammar: 相应 modifies 颜色 and refers to the colour assigned to each group. 应 is yìng in this correspondence sense.
note: 卡 kǎ means card here.

sentence: 借书表上写着“一号：《种花》；二号：《做饭》”；两个号码分别对应这两本书，我在借书单上写“二号”，老师就拿来了《做饭》。
grammar: 对应 takes the matching books as its object. The displayed list establishes which book each number identifies.
note: 分别 fēnbié means respectively here; 借书单 jièshūdān means a book-borrowing form.

sentence: 明天的车票我已经买好了；至于住哪儿，姐姐还在比较两家旅馆，今晚再告诉我。
grammar: 至于 shifts from the settled ticket purchase to the separate question of accommodation.
note: 旅馆 lǚguǎn means hotel or inn.

sentence: “我明天去图书馆。”“说到图书馆，你上周借的那本书还了吗？”
grammar: 说到 picks up 图书馆 from the preceding turn and introduces a related question about returning a book.

sentence: 我和姐姐正在商量搬家的安排；谈到要用的车，她说：“我的车太小，装不下那张桌子，得借一辆大的。”
grammar: 谈到 introduces the vehicle question within the moving discussion. It is another lexical way to introduce a topic, alongside 说到.

sentence: 老师提议把小组活动从下午改到晚上；对于这个安排，我有不同意见：我晚上要上课，希望活动还是下午两点开始。
grammar: 对于 identifies the arrangement toward which the speaker expresses a differing opinion. The following explanation states the scheduling conflict.

sentence: 从家到学校有三公里；对骑车的姐姐来说不算远，可爷爷只能走路，觉得太远。
grammar: In 对 + person + 来说, 来说 limits the evaluation to that person's perspective. The sister cycles, while the grandfather evaluates the same distance as someone who can only walk.

sentence: 我在给室友的留言里写道：“就房租而言，楼上这间更便宜，每月少两百元；但楼下那间有大窗户，住着更舒服。”
grammar: 而言 completes 就房租而言 and confines the lower-cost judgment to rent. The following comfort comparison concerns a different aspect.
register: 就……而言 suits this written comparison; 就……来说 is a common conversational alternative.

sentence: 这两间客房一间每晚一百元，一间一百五十元；就价格来说，我选一百元的，但还得看看床舒不舒服。
meaning: with regard to; in terms of
grammar: 就 introduces the aspect being considered in 就价格来说. The choice is limited to price and leaves comfort to be checked.

sentence: 生日聚会的分工已经定了：姐姐负责做饭；我呢，负责买饮料和接待客人。
grammar: 呢 follows 我 and marks it as a contrasting topic before the comment about the speaker's duties. It does not form a question here.

sentence: 我以为新来的同事不喜欢整理旧书，不会帮忙；他倒很热情，主动来问哪些书需要先收。
grammar: 倒 introduces the colleague's actual enthusiasm against the speaker's explicit expectation of unwillingness. This adverb is dào, not toppling dǎo.

sentence: 我在给两组同学的留言里写道：“摄影组在楼上整理照片，读书组则在楼下登记书本，做完后再一起收拾教室。”
grammar: 则 marks the second comment in a parallel comparison of the two groups' locations and tasks. It does not order one task after the other.
register: 则 is concise written wording for this parallel contrast.

sentence: 我刚开始学这门课，以为这道题只有老师会做；没想到连我也做对了，老师还请我解释答案。
grammar: 连 presents the novice speaker as an unexpectedly successful participant. Following 也 links that surprising member to the successful result.
note: 没想到 méi xiǎngdào means unexpectedly or to one's surprise.

sentence: 这间房除了房租还要交水电费；光房租就要三千元，可我每月的预算总共只有两千五百元，只好再找找。
grammar: 光 isolates rent from the larger housing expense. With 就, it emphasizes that this component alone already exceeds the available budget.
note: 水电费 shuǐdiànfèi means water and electricity charges.

sentence: 我们明天搬桌子，负责人说：“至少要来四个人，两个人抬一张，分两组同时搬；多来几个人也欢迎。”现在只有三个人答应，我还得再找人。
grammar: 至少 sets four people as the required lower bound. More are welcome, while the three confirmed participants do not yet meet the requirement.

sentence: 活动室的老师说：“每组最多借三把椅子，少借也可以。”我们只借了两把，已经够用。
grammar: 最多 sets an upper borrowing limit of three chairs. The actual loan is two, so the permitted maximum is not the actual quantity.

sentence: 昨天下课后，有个年轻人在教室门口等我；我不认识他，他先介绍了自己的名字，说想参加我们的读书组。
grammar: 有个 introduces an indefinite participant into the account. 个 classifies 年轻人, and subsequent 他 maintains reference to that person.
note: 年轻 niánqīng means young. 个 can weaken to neutral ge in unstressed speech.

sentence: 昨天有一位老师来参加读书会，还帮我们整理了书；那位老师今天又发来短信，说下周也能来。
grammar: 那位 resumes the teacher introduced in the first clause. 位 classifies the person; 那 refers backward in the account rather than indicating physical distance.

sentence: 昨晚我忘了锁活动室的门，后来老师看见门没锁，替我锁上了；这事提醒我，以后离开前要再检查一次。
grammar: 这事 refers back to the incident of leaving the door unlocked and the teacher securing it. The entire event becomes the topic of the following comment.

sentence: 老师教我记借书情况：先写借书人的名字，再写书名和还书日期；这样每本书借给了谁、哪天该还，都能查清楚。
grammar: 这样 refers to the stated recording procedure. The following clause explains what that procedure makes possible.
note: 书名 shūmíng means book title; 查 chá means check or consult records.

sentence: “我把所有书放进一个大箱子，最后再慢慢分。”“我不想那样收，怕找书麻烦；我先按大小分开，再装进几个小箱子。”
grammar: 那样 refers to the other speaker's procedure of packing everything together before sorting. The reply states a different procedure.

sentence: “楼上教室的桌子比楼下多，也更安静。”“桌子多，这一点我同意，楼上六张，楼下四张；不过楼上隔壁正在大声唱歌，我不觉得更安静。”
grammar: 这一点 singles out the claim about desk numbers. Agreement with that claim does not extend to the separate claim about quietness.
note: In connected speech, 一 normally becomes yì before third-tone diǎn.

sentence: 老师送来十本书，其中四本是字典，另外六本是故事书；我先把字典放进书柜，再给故事书登记。
grammar: 其中 refers to the established ten-book set. 四本 selects a subset, and the following six books account for the remainder.

sentence: 我给室友写了两个选择：修旧椅子，或者买新椅子；前者只花二十元，但要等三天，买新的今天就能用，得花一百元。
meaning: the former; the first of the two
grammar: 前者 refers to the first listed option, repairing the old chair. It does not refer to a physically nearer chair.
register: Common in written comparisons; conversation often repeats the first option's name.

sentence: 我在给老师的回复里写：“您提的两个安排，一个是看短片，一个是轮流介绍自己带的书；我选后者，想介绍我昨天刚读完的故事书。”
meaning: the latter; the second of the two
grammar: 后者 selects the second listed arrangement, introducing participants' books. The speaker's planned book introduction confirms that reference.
register: Common in written comparisons; conversation often repeats the second option's name.

sentence: 今天收到了八份报名表，我先核对了两份，地址都写全了；其余六份还没看，等吃完午饭再继续。
grammar: 其余 identifies all six forms left after the two checked forms are excluded from the eight-form set.

sentence: 桌上三本种花的书，我只读过红封面那本，别的都没读过；你先给我讲讲另外两本吧。
grammar: 别的 stands for the other gardening books, with 书 understood from the three-book set. 都 applies to the two remaining books.

sentence: 今天六个人一起准备生日聚会，姐姐和我去买菜，其他四个人留在家里收拾房间；晚饭前我们再一起摆桌子。
grammar: 其他 modifies 四个人 and identifies the participants outside the named pair. The pair and the four remaining participants make up the six-person group.

sentence: 这十张旧照片，三张背面写着日期；另一些的日期我还记得，准备写上；还有两张，我想不起来是哪天拍的，得问姐姐。
grammar: 另一些 selects an additional plural subset of the photographs. It does not include the final two photographs whose dates the speaker cannot recall.
note: 一些 yīxiē means some; 另 indicates an additional subset.

sentence: 这次借书活动，我和姐姐分别负责登记书名和核对借书人的姓名：我把书名写进表格，姐姐拿名单核对名字。
grammar: 分别 pairs the first participant with the first task and the second participant with the second task. The explanation explicitly confirms both assignments.

sentence: 我和姐姐上同一门课，各自的课本上却写着不同的笔记；她记了词的意思，我记了句子的用法。
grammar: 各自 precedes 的 and identifies the textbook associated with each participant. It modifies the noun phrase rather than directly distributing an action.
note: 笔记 bǐjì means notes; 用法 yòngfǎ means usage.

sentence: 我和室友交换了电话号码：我存了她的，她存了我的；现在有事都能直接联系彼此。
grammar: 彼此 refers reciprocally to the two roommates: the speaker can contact the roommate, and the roommate can contact the speaker.
note: 交换 jiāohuàn means exchange; 存 cún means save or store. In connected speech, bǐ normally rises to bí before third-tone cǐ.

sentence: 我问同事：“周五下午能帮我接待客人吗？”对方回答：“三点以后可以，三点以前我要上课。”我便把接待时间定在三点半。
grammar: 对方 refers to the colleague addressed by the speaker. The quoted reply belongs to that other participant in the exchange.
note: 便 biàn here means then or consequently.

sentence: 我在给老师的留言里写道：“摄影组和读书组原来都想周六下午用教室；后来改为摄影组上午用、读书组下午用，双方都同意这个安排。”
grammar: 双方 includes the photography group and the reading group as the two parties to the arrangement. 都 distributes agreement across both groups.

sentence: 我问老师能不能替姐姐介绍她读过的书。老师说：“我们想听她自己的看法，请本人来讲吧，你可以陪她来。”
grammar: 本人 identifies the sister whose own reading views are wanted. The proposed substitute may accompany her but is not the requested speaker.

sentence: 弟弟小安要在读书会上介绍一本书，妈妈怕他紧张，想让我替他讲；我说：“还是让他自己讲吧，我可以在旁边帮忙。”
grammar: 他自己 emphasizes the younger brother as the person who should speak, contrasting him with the proposed substitute. Help from someone nearby remains possible.
note: 紧张 jǐnzhāng means nervous.

sentence: 这次读书会，写书的林老师原来让同事替他介绍新书；后来他亲自来了，说想直接听听大家的问题。
grammar: 亲自 marks the author's own attendance, contrasting with the original plan for a colleague to introduce the book on his behalf.

sentence: 新买的椅子送到时，外面的纸箱破了；椅子本身没有受损，四条腿都结实，坐着也稳，我就没有退货。
grammar: 本身 confines the damage assessment to the chair itself, excluding the damaged outer carton.
note: 纸箱 zhǐxiāng means cardboard carton.

sentence: 我写的故事里，小安搬到了河湾镇，刚到时不认识路，就请当地人告诉他学校在哪里。
grammar: 当地 refers to the town already named in the story and modifies 人. It does not automatically mean the narrator's present location.
note: 镇 zhèn means town. 河湾镇 Héwān Zhèn is the town in the speaker's story.

sentence: 我上小学时住在学校旁边，当年每天走两分钟就到教室；现在工作了，去公司要坐半个小时公交车。
grammar: 当年 recalls the earlier primary-school period, contrasting its short walk with the present commute. Here dāngnián means back then, rather than in that same calendar year.
note: 小学 xiǎoxué means primary school.

sentence: 上周五上午，我提交了报名表，当天下午就收到老师的确认短信，晚上把活动时间告诉了姐姐。
grammar: 当天 refers to the Friday already specified, so the confirmation arrives that Friday afternoon rather than the following day.
note: 当 has fourth tone in this selected same-day reading.

sentence: 姐姐说：“我回家要坐一个小时的车，不想把课改到晚上。”我回家也要坐一个小时，同样不愿意改，我们就一起向老师说明了原因。
grammar: 同样 applies the sister's unwillingness to the speaker under the same travel constraint. 改 refers to the already stated change to evening classes.

sentence: 我们原来约好周六三点在我家读书，姐姐带书，我准备茶；她提议改到四点，我那时要出门，最后商量好照旧。
grammar: 照旧 means retain the previous arrangement. The earlier clauses supply the time, place and division of responsibilities.

sentence: 我们每周六都在家里轮流读一段课文；这周姐姐出差，用电话跟我们一起读，活动照样进行，没有停。
grammar: 照样 says the established activity continues despite the changed circumstance. The sister participates by telephone rather than being present.
note: 进行 jìnxíng means take place or proceed.

sentence: 老师交代：“最后离开时关窗、锁门，钥匙放进门边的盒子。”我照办了，走前又检查了一遍，窗和门都关好了。
grammar: 照办 takes the preceding instructions as understood content. 了 reports that the speaker carried them out.

sentence: 姐姐示范收书的方法：先把字典放在左边，再把故事书放在右边；我照做，很快把自己桌上的书也分好了。
meaning: do as shown; follow the method
grammar: 照做 refers to following the demonstrated method. The two placement steps establish what the speaker follows.
note: 示范 shìfàn means demonstrate how to do something.

sentence: 我们已经约好明天三点在图书馆门口见；我本来想发“明天三点在图书馆门口见”，后来省略了已说好的地点，只发“明天三点见”。
